subject: EdgePay TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up and test plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgepay.com>, Ingram Patel <ingram@edgepay.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: EdgePay TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up and test plan

Hi Alyssa / Ingram —

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call + an actionable plan to validate your TTFT and streaming cadence requirements. I captured the numbers you called out and a proposed validation approach below.

Key targets you mentioned
- TTFT target: <= 120 ms (median) for the initial token on standard chat prompts (50–150 tokens)
- Sustained concurrency: 400 concurrent interactive sessions (peak 650)
- Request throughput target: ~60 req/sec sustained during payment batch windows
- Streaming preference: SSE for browser clients; WebSocket acceptable for mobile apps
- Chunk cadence: prefer smaller, frequent chunks (aim 40–80ms between chunks, grouping ~3–6 tokens) to keep UI feeling live

Proposed validation plan (pilot scope)
1) Pilot infrastructure: Dedicated small pool (4x A100-equivalent) for EdgePay, instrumented with token-level traces.
2) Synthetic test matrix:
   - Latency-only: single-session warm/cold measurements to capture cold TTFT vs steady-state (100 cold runs, 1k warm runs).
   - Concurrency ramp: step from 50 -> 400 -> 650 concurrent sessions, hold 10 minutes at each step.
   - Streaming cadence: run SSE clients with payloads matching your UI (see attached payload samples) and measure chunk inter-arrival distribution.
   - Throughput burst: 60 req/sec sustained for 30 minutes; include a 200 req/sec 2-minute burst to validate autoscaling/fallback.
3) Success criteria:
   - Median TTFT <= 120 ms; 95th percentile < 250 ms under 400 conc.
   - Chunk inter-arrival median between 40–80 ms; no more than 10% of user-visible chunks exceeding 200 ms in steady-state.
   - No dropped streaming connections at 400 conc; graceful fallback to polling for WebSocket clients if underlying capacity is exceeded.
4) Observability and artifacts: detailed token traces, per-route latency histograms, and a Spike playbook with recommended fallback thresholds.

Next steps I recommend for this week
- EdgePay to confirm the sample prompts (attached) and client distribution (browser vs mobile %).
- We’ll provision the dedicated pool and schedule the pilot for Tuesday (2026-06-16) if that works.
- Post-pilot sync to review traces and agree on any SLO adjustments.

I attached a short PDF with the requirements we noted and sample payloads. If the targets above change, call them out and I’ll rework the plan.

Thanks —
Markus

Thanks Markus — this is great and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 120 ms TTFT we stated is for keynote checkout flows (high priority). For lower-priority admin flows we can tolerate up to 300 ms.
- Client distribution: 72% web (SSE), 22% mobile (WebSocket), 6% server-to-server (no streaming).
- We have some prompts that include up to 300 tokens (long receipts + contextual history), so please include a small subset of longer prompts in the pilot.

Tuesday the 16th works for a morning slot PST. Please provision the pool and share test harness access. Ingram, can you confirm the SRE team can open a monitoring window that day?

Cheers,
Alyssa

Perfect — thanks for the distribution breakdown, Alyssa. A couple of operational notes before we kick off: 

- We added the long-prompt set to the payloads (see streaming_payload_samples.json).
- Provisioning: I’ve queued Dedicated pool EP-2209-dedicated-01 (4x A100-eq). ETA: ~3 hours to be ready for test harness access.
- Observability: you’ll get a read-only Grafana link and token-level traces exported to the shared Drive link.

Operational fallback & canary policy
- Canary mode: first run at 20% of target concurrency on the dedicated pool to validate chunk cadence behavior, then ramp to 100%.
- Fallback: if 95th TTFT > 350 ms during canary, we’ll immediately throttle to smaller batching sizes and fallback client-side to polling for non-critical flows.

Test harness credentials and the Grafana link are attached below. I’ll be on the runbook channel during the window.

Next steps (concrete)
- Markus: provisioned pool and test harness by 10:30 PDT today.
- EdgePay: confirm SRE monitoring window and any IP allowlist.
- Both: 11:00 PDT post-run sync to review traces and agree pass/fail.

Markus

Subject: Internal: EdgePay pilot notes & checklist (do not forward)

Internal checklist after today's run (captured during post-run sync):
- Cold TTFTs for long prompts were higher than expected (median 240 ms). Record indicates cold worker spin-up contributed ~80 ms.
- Warm steady-state median TTFT for checkout flows: 110 ms (meets target). 95th at 190 ms under 400 conc (ok).
- SSE chunk cadence median 55 ms, but saw occasional spikes at ~320 ms correlated with GC pauses on the app process on one node.
- Connection churn: ~0.6% during peak; investigation pointed to transient NAT timeouts on EdgePay side.

Immediate recommended actions for next sprint:
- Add a small warm pool (keep-alive capacity) to absorb cold spin-up for high-priority flows.
- Tune runtime GC/windowing on the affected node and re-run chunk-cadence focused test.
- EdgePay SRE: whitelist our egress IPs and verify NAT timeout settings.

I documented traces and the run artifacts in the shared Drive link and flagged two follow-up action items as a HubSpot task under EP-2209.

Sergio
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
